scope: final round: patch incomingSequence before sending the gamestate

verified_facts.patch_result: conn+0x34 written to 2, verified by read-back
verified_facts.start_challenge_result: {"status":"challenge_armed"} with ring_b still 0/0 and no fragment logged
verified_facts.meaning: start-challenge only arms the challenge; it does not cause our server to emit the gamestate

the_ordering_paradox.problem: the gamestate is only produced when 'forward' runs against our server, but forward performs its own connect and resets the connection state we just patched
the_ordering_paradox.consequence: patching before forward is undone; patching after forward is too late because the fragments were already consumed
solution_candidates: patch during the forward window: start forward in the background, poll status for a populated connection, patch conn+0x34 immediately, then trigger a second gamestate emission (forward again or a dedicated send command)
or make our server send the gamestate twice: first frame gets dropped under the wrong sequence, second frame arrives after the patch
or add a server mode that waits N seconds after connect before emitting, giving us time to patch

status_of_the_sequence_hypothesis.supporting_evidence: conn+0x34 read 1 in two independent populated runs, and the reference server's first in-band sequence was 3 after a real handshake
status_of_the_sequence_hypothesis.what_would_settle_it: the patch-then-send ordering described above, with stage/messageAck as the readout
